{"self_assessment": "Impact: Our table's fish came out fully connected, with all 113 standing dominoes knocked over from the start, nose to both tail points. I fetched a tray of dominoes and laid 14 on the top line near the middle of the upper curve, where the line runs into the doubled section. I also checked the run from the start several times, so the table could trust the whole fish would carry through.

Execution: I put my time into verification. I inspected the doubled section, the nose and the tail bend repeatedly, and confirmed the whole run carried from the start before the push. I advised that the sharp corner at the tail tip needed a smooth re-lay rather than a connect, and that was the approach taken. I kept my hands off the build once it was complete, so nothing got bumped before the push.

Collaboration: I split the work to avoid crowding, staying clear of teammates' areas so we didn't bump each other. I coordinated the handoff on the top line, gave Jack specific guidance on the tail join, and checked in with Omar on the bottom line. I kept messages short and actionable.

Leadership: I proposed the sequencing, with top line first, then joins, then a full-run check, and I called for hands off once the fish was verified. I stayed straightforward about where the weak spots were, which kept the team focused on the one real risk. I believe my contribution was a meaningful part of a strong team result, alongside the others' work on the bottom line, the tail and the supply.", "my_share_percent": 20}
